# Communicating with the community {.unnumbered}

This section will introduce communication practices, resources, and pathways for coordinating work and building effective relationships with other community members.

## The Bioconductor Chat

Bioconductor uses the open source team chat [Zulip](https://zulip.com/).
The platform is freely accessible.
New users can sign up for at <https://chat.bioconductor.org/>.

::: {.callout-note}
The community previously used Slack for chat, but the transition to Zulip was made to ensure long-term access to discussions and better reflect the community's open-source values.
You can read more about the move from Slack to Zulip - which took place on Monday 2 June 2025 - in the Bioconductor blog post [Bioconductor is Moving from Slack to Zulip for Community Chat](https://blog.bioconductor.org/posts/2025-05-29-slack-to-zulip/).
:::

The Bioconductor Zulip chat is intended for real-time, informal discussion and collaboration within the community, including quick questions, coordination, and exchanging ideas.
For technical questions that would benefit from a searchable, persistent answer, the *Bioconductor Support Site* remains the preferred venue (see below).

## The Bioconductor Support Site

The Bioconductor Support Site is a forum for asking questions and sharing knowledge about Bioconductor packages and workflows.
The site is hosted at <https://support.bioconductor.org>.

Questions and answers are publicly searchable and persistent - without the need to create an account or log in - making it a valuable resource for the community.
